name: PARAGUAY

flag.title: Tri-sided wonder
flag.note: Only flag with a unique design on each side

lead: Paraguay is in the middle of South America and has no sea. A river splits it in two. Almost everyone speaks Spanish and Guaraní. The giant Itaipu Dam powers the whole country with water.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: The Paraguay River cuts the country in half. The east is green and hilly, and most people live there. Farmers grow soya beans in red soil.
The west is the Gran Chaco, a wild plain of thorny forest. It covers 60% of the land. Fewer people live there than in a small town.
animals: The giant anteater walks the Chaco on its knuckles. It slurps 35,000 ants a day through a tube-like snout. Jaguars pad through the night.
The capybara is the world's largest rodent, as big as a big dog. It wallows in Paraguay's wetlands. Over 500 bird species live here, including the hyacinth macaw.
culture: Paraguay is one of few countries where nearly everyone speaks an indigenous language daily. Guaraní rings out in markets, songs, and jokes. The Paraguayan harp plays at every celebration.
Sharing tereré (ice-cold herbal tea) is as important as a handshake. Friends pass one shared cup around a circle. Ñandutí is lace that means 'spider web'.
history: Paraguay broke from Spain on 14 May 1811 without a shot. The War of the Triple Alliance (1864–70) was against Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay. It killed about half the people and nearly 90% of adult men.
Paraguay beat Bolivia in the Chaco War (1932–35). Stroessner ruled as dictator from 1954 to 1989. His rule ended peacefully, and democracy has held ever since.
wows: Paraguay's flag is the only one worldwide with a different emblem on each side.
Itaipu Dam set a 2016 world record: 103 terawatt-hours (huge power) in one year.
Paraguay has no coast, yet the largest navy of any country without one.
Pistol duelling is still legal if both duelists are blood donors.
Paraguay cooked a Guinness record barbecue for about 30,000 people.
About 90% of Paraguayans mix Spanish and Guaraní, called Jopará.
Paraguay makes nearly 100% of its electricity from water.

myths.fact: Giant anteaters have no teeth at all. Their sticky tongue can be 60 cm long.

myths.myth: A jaguar is just a leopard
myths.fact: Jaguars live in the Americas, leopards in Africa and Asia. Jaguars are chunkier and love to swim.
